reference: Fringe benefits tax regime is essentially a tax on a wide range of benefits provided by an employer to an employee. This tax is payable by the employer, not the employee, because the benefit is received from the employment. There are a number of different types of fringe benefit, which all fall within these two categories.In this case, the fringe benefit is taxable because it falls within one of these two categories. A de minimis benefit is a minor, trivial benefit that can be given to an employee without it being classified as a fringe benefit. It is called a de minimis benefit because the value of the benefit is so small that it is unimportant. In practice, de minimis benefits are usually related to the workplace, such as a birthday cake or a cup of coffee. They are not subject to FBT because they are not significant enough to constitute a benefit.A benefit that is given to supervisory employees is also taxable. These benefits are treated differently under the FBTAA because they are given to employees who have some level of responsibility for managing other employees.Benefits provided to rank and file employees are also taxable. These benefits are generally given to employees who do not have any level of responsibility for managing other employees.Benefits given in the form of insurance or retirement benefits plan are also taxable.An employer may provide an employee with a range of benefits from which the employee chooses the benefit that best suits the employee’s needs. For example, an employee might be able to choose between an additional week of annual leave and a one-off payment of $5000.The option e is the correct answer because it supports employees education. This is a taxable fringe benefit. Employers are encouraged to provide educational assistance to their employees because it helps to increase the skill levels of the workforce and improve productivity.
